injection.affected: auth.py (sqlite3 string-concatenated queries, e.g. login L97, check_balance L132, transfer L158-166), app.py (psycopg2 queries built via f-strings/`%`), transaction_graphql.py (f-string SQL at L46/78/106/155), merchant_payments.py
injection.approach: Use parameterized queries everywhere: psycopg2 `cursor.execute(sql, params)` with `%s` placeholders and sqlite3 with `?` placeholders. Never interpolate user input into SQL/template/command strings. For template injection, keep Jinja2 autoescaping enabled and never render user-controlled template strings; avoid `eval`/`exec`/dynamic `import`.

database-security.affected: database.py (connection pool authenticates as the Postgres superuser `postgres`), docker-compose.yml (postgres:13 service, POSTGRES_USER=postgres)
database-security.approach: Create a dedicated least-privilege application DB role, parameterize queries, bound result-set sizes, validate the connection string, and restrict the application's DB grants to only the tables/operations it needs.

authentication.affected: auth.py (hardcoded JWT_SECRET='secret123', ALGORITHMS includes 'none', verify_token falls back to verify_signature:false), app.py (forgot/reset use random.randint for the reset PIN, default admin/admin123 seeded in database.py), merchant_payments.py (predictable 4-digit-derived API key)
authentication.approach: Load the JWT secret from a secret store/env var, restrict algorithms to a single strong symmetric/asymmetric alg (remove 'none' and the no-verify fallback), generate reset PINs/API keys with `secrets`, enforce account lockout/throttling, and remove all default/seeded credentials.

authorization.affected: app.py (IDOR: /check_balance, /transfer, /api/virtual-cards/<id>/*, /api/bill-payments accept account/card/user identifiers without verifying ownership), transaction_graphql.py (_resolve_scope), auth.py (token_required)
authorization.approach: Enforce server-side, deny-by-default authorization on every object access: verify the authenticated principal owns or is permitted the requested resource before acting. Centralize authorization checks and apply least privilege.

xss.affected: templates/*.html (Jinja2), static/dashboard.js and static/merchant.js (client-side DOM rendering)
xss.approach: Keep Jinja2 autoescaping enabled and contextually escape all untrusted output; avoid `innerHTML`/unsafe DOM sinks in JS; send a Content-Security-Policy and `X-Frame-Options: DENY` (or CSP frame-ancestors) to block injection and clickjacking.

csrf.approach: Add anti-CSRF tokens to state-changing requests (e.g. Flask-WTF CSRFProtect or a synchronizer token), use `SameSite` cookies, and restrict each route to the correct HTTP methods.

cors.affected: app.py L35 `CORS(app)` enables permissive cross-origin access globally
cors.approach: Scope CORS to an explicit allowlist of trusted origins, methods and headers; never combine a wildcard origin with credentials.

ssrf.affected: app.py /upload_profile_picture_url (fetches an attacker-supplied URL), the emulated /latest/meta-data/* IMDS routes
ssrf.approach: Validate and allowlist outbound destinations, reject internal/link-local/metadata IP ranges, restrict URL scheme to http(s), and disable following redirects to private hosts.

crypto.affected: auth.py (HS256 with weak hardcoded secret), merchant_payments.py (`hashlib.sha256` over a 4-digit code for API keys), app.py (`random.randint` reset PIN)
crypto.approach: Use approved algorithms and key lengths, generate all tokens/PINs/keys with the `secrets` module, never use fast hashes for secrets, and protect data in transit with TLS.

session-management.affected: auth.py (JWT accepted from header/args/form/cookies), static/dashboard.js (JWT in localStorage)
session-management.approach: Issue unique session identifiers, set `Secure`/`HttpOnly`/`SameSite` on session cookies, expire/invalidate sessions on logout, and never place tokens/session IDs in URLs.

file-handling.approach: Validate file content/type (not just extension), store with randomized server-generated names outside the web root or with restricted execution, prevent path traversal/symlink following, and clean up temporary files.

api-security.affected: app.py /api/* REST endpoints and /graphql, transaction_graphql.py (graphene schema)
api-security.approach: Enforce authentication and per-object authorization on every endpoint, return only required fields, throttle requests, cap request/response sizes, and for GraphQL limit query depth/complexity, disable batching abuse and disable introspection in production.

secrets-config.affected: auth.py (JWT_SECRET), docker-compose.yml and .env.example (DB_PASSWORD), database.py (seeded admin/admin123), app.py (Flask debug=True via start.sh)
secrets-config.approach: Move all secrets to environment variables/a secret manager, remove default accounts and passwords, and ship secure-by-default configuration (debug disabled).

logging-monitoring.affected: app.py (debug_info with IP/User-Agent returned in responses, `print` statements, Flask debug=True)
logging-monitoring.approach: Use structured logging, never return debug/stack data to clients, redact sensitive fields, protect log access, and disable debug mode in production.

dependency-management.approach: Pin and patch dependencies to current secure versions, enable automated dependency/vulnerability scanning, and review transitive dependencies.

network-infra.affected: Deployment topology (Flask development server on port 5000, no TLS/reverse proxy in repo)
network-infra.approach: These controls require infrastructure not present in the repository (reverse proxy/WAF, TLS termination, network segmentation, HTTP request-smuggling protections). Document the required infrastructure change.

backup-recovery.affected: No backup/restore tooling exists in the repository
backup-recovery.approach: Backup, restore and re-deployment routines are operational/infrastructure controls with no corresponding code in this repository. Document the required process and infrastructure.

data-protection.affected: database.py (virtual_cards.cvv and users.password stored in plaintext; PII in users), static/dashboard.js (JWT in localStorage)
data-protection.approach: Encrypt sensitive data at rest, never store card CVV, salt+hash passwords, and avoid keeping long-lived secrets in browser storage.

input-validation.affected: app.py request handlers (JSON/form/query input used without validation)
input-validation.approach: Validate and normalize all server-side input against strict allowlists/schemas before use; never trust client-supplied values for security decisions.

llm-security.affected: ai_agent_deepseek.py (system_prompt explicitly instructs the model to obey injected instructions and expose the database; _get_database_context runs DB queries from user text; no output filtering), app.py /api/ai/chat and /api/ai/chat/anonymous
llm-security.approach: For code-applicable LLM risks: rewrite the system prompt to refuse injected/override instructions, sanitize and bound user input, filter/escape model output before returning or rendering it, run the agent with a least-privilege read-only DB role, and rate-limit. For risks tied to model training/fine-tuning/vector-stores/model-theft: the app calls an external DeepSeek API and does not train, host, fine-tune or vector-index models, so these are documented as not code-fixable in this repository.

general-hardening.approach: Ensure resources (DB connections, file handles) are released promptly in finally blocks to prevent exhaustion.
